title: feat: estimate missing calories from power/HR data
description:
## Summary

Some devices — most notably the Hammerhead Karoo — don't write `total_calories` to their FIT files. After uploading, Garmin Connect shows the activity with 0 kcal, which also skews daily calorie totals and the nutrition module. This PR adds an opt-in, per-profile feature that estimates the missing value from data already recorded in the file and writes it into the Session and Lap messages.

Full transparency: this change was vibe-coded with Claude Code — but every part of it was reviewed, tested against real FIT files from my own rides, and the uploaded results were verified in Garmin Connect.

## How it works

A new `calorie_calculator.py` module supports two methods, in order of preference:

1. **Power-based** (used when at least 50% of records carry valid power data):
   integrates mechanical work from the power samples and converts kJ → kcal
   assuming 22% gross efficiency (`1 kJ ≈ 1.086 kcal`), the same convention
   used by Hammerhead, Garmin, and Strava. No personal data needed.
2. **HR-based fallback**: the Keytel et al. (2005) regression, which needs
   weight, age, and sex (stored in the profile, used for nothing else).

The estimation is defensive by design:

- **existing calorie values are never overwritten** — only missing ones are
  filled in,
- power is integrated trapezoidally (mean of the interval endpoints), which stays accurate for sparse "smart recording" samples,
- if the power meter drops out mid-ride, the affected samples fall back to the HR method (when weight/age/sex are configured) instead of counting zero work; the log message reports how many samples were filled this way,
- implausible samples are rejected (power > 2000 W, HR outside 30–230 bpm, FIT "invalid" markers),
- recording gaps are clamped to 30 s so pauses don't inflate the total,
- the session total is split across laps (samples falling between laps are attributed to the next lap to start), renormalized so the lap values sum up exactly to the session total,
- if neither method is applicable, the file is processed as before and a warning is logged.

Writing the value required a small workaround in `fit_editor.py`: when the source file's definition message doesn't include `total_calories`, the field is not growable in `fit_tool`, so the editor flips the flag and resets the cached definition so `FitFileBuilder(auto_define=True)` regenerates it.

## Configuration / UI

- New `Profile` fields: `recalculate_calories`, `weight_kg`, `age`, `sex` (all optional; existing configs load unchanged, no migration needed).
- New optional step in the profile creation wizard, plus full support in the edit wizard: values are pre-filled, Enter keeps them, and answering "No" to the weight/age/sex question removes them from the profile. Disabling the feature keeps the stored values so re-enabling doesn't ask for them again.
- The profiles table (`--list-profiles` / TUI) got a "Kcal est." column showing which profiles have the feature enabled.
- Weight can be entered in kg or lbs.

## Tests

- Full suite passing (324 tests); coverage for `config.py` and `app.py` stays at 100%.
- New `tests/test_calorie_calculator.py` (14 tests): power integration math, trapezoidal integration, single-sample and extended power dropouts (with and without HR data), HR fallback, method selection, gap clamping, per-lap split consistency including samples falling between or before laps.
- `tests/test_fit_editor.py`: end-to-end test on a real Karoo file (calories get injected and survive a rebuild/re-parse round trip) and a guard test proving existing calories are not touched (Zwift file).
- `tests/test_config.py`: new profile fields, legacy config compatibility, wizard flows including clearing anthropometric data, profiles table.

## Docs

- New "Calorie Estimation" section in the Multi-Profile Guide (motivation, both methods, dropout behaviour, config field reference) plus a new wizard step in the flow description and updated example config JSON.
- Short mention with a link in `README.md` / `docs/index.md`.
- `AGENTS.md` updated with the new module.

title: Keep device identity for unmodified manufacturers and add missing creator device_info — fixes #87
description:
Fixes #87.

## Problem
Files from apps that already identify as Garmin (e.g. TrainerDay: `manufacturer: garmin`,
`garmin_product: edge_530`, no `device_info`) reach Garmin Connect with no device:

1. `rewrite_file_id_message()` builds a new `FileIdMessage` but only sets `manufacturer`/`product`
   when `_should_modify_manufacturer()` is true. For other manufacturers the output has no
   manufacturer or product and a replaced serial, contrary to the docstring ("returned unchanged").
2. Without any `device_info` for the recording device, Garmin Connect has no creator device to show.

## Fix
- `rewrite_file_id_message()`: for manufacturers that aren't rewritten, copy the original
  `manufacturer`, `product` and `serial_number` and return early, matching the documented behaviour.
- `edit_fit()`: pre-scan for a creator `device_info` (`device_index` 0/unset, `device_type` != 0).
  If there is none, add one after `file_id` built from its manufacturer, product, serial and
  `time_created` (`device_index=0`, `source_type=local`). New helper `_build_creator_device_info()`.

Files that already have a creator `device_info` (Garmin devices, Karoo, etc.) are unaffected.

## Testing
- Two regression tests in `tests/test_fit_editor.py` (`TestGarminFileIdWithoutDeviceInfo`):
  identity preserved, and creator `device_info` added.
- Full suite: all pass except `test_show_dirs_flag_with_garmin_dirs`, which also fails on
  unmodified `main` in my environment.
- Real device: four TrainerDay rides (Aug 31 – Oct 13, 2026) deleted from Garmin Connect and
  re-uploaded. Before: no device. After: device shows as Edge 530.

## Note
Independent of #86 (COROS DURA). Both add a helper next to `_should_modify_device_info()`,
so whichever merges second may need a trivial conflict resolution there; happy to rebase.

title: Fix device_info rewrite for devices that omit product (COROS DURA) — fixes #80
description:
Fixes #80.

## Problem
The COROS DURA writes a `device_info` record containing only `manufacturer` (294)
and a text `product_name`. It has no numeric `product`, `device_index`,
`serial_number`, or `source_type`. The existing rewrite only overwrites `product`
when it is already present, so the output has `manufacturer=GARMIN` with no product,
and Garmin Connect shows no device for the activity.

Simply removing the `is not None` guard isn't enough: a parsed message's fields are
bound to the source definition, so assigning a field that wasn't defined raises
`Field is not growable`.

## Fix
When a `device_info` record being modified has no `product`/`garmin_product`:
- Rebuild it as a fresh `DeviceInfoMessage` (same approach as the `FileIdMessage`
  rewrite), copying all populated fields across.
- Set `product` to the profile's target device.
- Fill `device_index=0` (creator), `source_type=local`, and `serial_number` (from the
  profile, falling back to the existing default) if absent, so Garmin Connect
  recognises the record as the recording device.

Records that already carry a product (e.g. Hammerhead Karoo) go through the existing
code path unchanged.

## Testing
- Two regression tests added in `tests/test_fit_editor.py` (synthetic DURA-style files).
- Full suite: all pass except `test_show_dirs_flag_with_garmin_dirs`, which also fails
  on unmodified `main` in my environment.
- Real device: re-uploaded a COROS DURA activity (Aug 4, 2026). Before: no device in
  Garmin Connect. After: shows Edge 830. Karoo activities upload unchanged (409
  duplicate as expected).

Support Garmin MFA login and add .fit suffix to temp upload files
description:
Hello,
While running Fit-File-Faker on a fresh MyWhoosh profile I hit two issues:

### 1. MFA login support
`Garmin(email, password)` was constructed without a `prompt_mfa` callback. When Garmin's SSO required an MFA code, the underlying library raised:

```
GarminConnectAuthenticationError: MFA Required but no prompt_mfa mechanism supplied
```
I added a `prompt_mfa` callback that uses `questionary` (already a project dependency) to interactively ask the user for the one-time code. After a successful login, tokens are cached as before, so subsequent runs don't re-prompt.

## 2. Temp files must carry the `.fit` extension
Fix for:
```GarminConnectInvalidFileFormatError: File has no extension: /var/folders/g9/401mxzxx7cj89pmjyvmnw5c00000gn/T/tmp2g2z9cmi```

`garminconnect` validates the file extension in `upload_activity()` and rejects files without one. I added `suffix=".fit"` to both `NamedTemporaryFile(...)` calls in `upload_all()` and `NewFileEventHandler.on_created()`.

title: feat: replace garth with garminconnect for Garmin Connect uploads
description:
## Background

Garmin changed their authentication flow to use Cloudflare TLS fingerprinting, which blocks `garth`'s mobile user-agent (`GCM-iOS-5.7.2.1`). This prevents OAuth tokens from being created, breaking all uploads. Also, as of now, the `garth` project is effectively archived and so we should no longer rely on it.

This PR swaps out garth with `python-garminconnect` for authentication and uploading files.

Closes #75.

## Changes

- **Dependency swap**: `garth>=0.5.21` → `garminconnect>=0.3.3`
- **`get_garth_dir()` → `get_token_dir()`**: Token storage moved from `user_cache_path` to `user_data_path` so tokens survive routine cache wipes; directory prefix changes from `.garth_<name>` to `.garmin_<name>`
- **`upload()` rewritten**: Uses `Garmin(email, password).login(tokenstore=...)` + `upload_activity()`; raises `ValueError` immediately for missing credentials instead of prompting interactively
- **`--show-dirs`**: Now shows the data directory and lists `.garmin_*` token directories
- **Logging**: Removed `oauth1_auth` logger suppression (garth-specific)
- **Tests**: Replaced `mock_garth_*` fixtures with `mock_garmin_client`; updated show-dirs tests for new directory names and locations

## Upgrade behavior for users

- Re-authentication happens automatically on first run after upgrade (no manual steps required)
- Existing `.garth_*` directories are left behind as orphaned dirs; they cause no harm but can be manually deleted
- `garminconnect` automatically falls back through multiple login strategies if rate-limited (429), so auth is resilient

## Test plan

- [x] All 287 tests pass
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass
- [x] Manual smoke test: `fit-file-faker -u -d tests/files/mywhoosh_20260111.fit` authenticated successfully via `widget+cffi` fallback strategy
- [x] Full upload test: `fit-file-faker -u tests/files/mywhoosh_20260111.fit` uploaded successfully to Garmin Connect
- [x] Token cached to `~/Library/Application Support/FitFileFaker/.garmin_<profile>/garmin_tokens.json`

- Add note that Garmin Connect method may not work for all device types

fix: UTF-8 Decoding Errors and Add Serial Number Documentation
description:
## Summary

Resolves #65 

This PR addresses a bug where FIT files with non-UTF-8 encoded strings (e.g., from Zwift using Windows-1252/Latin-1 encoding) would fail to process with `UnicodeDecodeError`. It also adds comprehensive documentation about the importance of serial numbers for Garmin Connect feature compatibility.

## Changes

### Bug Fix: Non-UTF-8 String Handling

- **Modified `fit_file_faker/utils.py`**: Added `_lenient_read_strings_from_bytes()` function that implements a multi-strategy string decoding approach:
  1. Attempts UTF-8 decoding (FIT specification standard)
  2. Falls back to Latin-1/ISO-8859-1 for common Windows encodings
  3. Uses replacement characters as last resort
- **Applied the patch**: Integrated the lenient decoder into the `apply_fit_tool_patch()` function
- **Impact**: Tool can now process FIT files from devices that don't strictly follow UTF-8 encoding (seen on Zwift and maybe some other platforms)

### Documentation Enhancements

Added critical warnings and guidance about serial number validation across all documentation:

- **CLAUDE.md**: Added detailed section on serial number behavior and Garmin Connect recognition
- **README.md**: Added new "⚠️ Important: Device Serial Numbers" section explaining:
  - Why serial numbers must match device types
  - Impact on Training Effect, challenges, badges, and Training Status
  - Recommendations for using real device serial numbers vs. random generation
  - What functionality is affected by invalid serial numbers
- **docs/developer-guide.md**: Added developer-focused documentation on serial number implementation

### User Experience Improvements

- **Modified `fit_file_faker/config.py`**: 
  - Added warning messages during profile creation/editing about serial number implications
  - Improved instructions for finding device serial numbers (both on-device and in Garmin Connect)
  - Reordered serial number options to recommend custom entry over random generation

### Testing

- **Added test file**: `tests/files/zwift_non_utf8_20260130.fit` - Real-world Zwift file with non-UTF-8 strings
- **Added fixture**: `zwift_non_utf8_fit_parsed` for testing the fix
- **Enhanced tests**: 
  - `test_fit_editor.py`: Added test case for non-UTF-8 file processing
  - `test_utils.py`: Comprehensive test suite (97 new lines) covering:
    - Normal UTF-8 decoding
    - Latin-1 fallback behavior
    - Replacement character handling
    - Edge case exception paths
    - Lenient field length calculations

## Testing

- ✅ All existing tests pass
- ✅ New test file (Zwift with non-UTF-8 strings) processes successfully
- ✅ Comprehensive unit tests for both UTF-8 and Latin-1 decoding paths
- ✅ Edge case handling verified

description:

## Changes

### Core Features

description:
Hello,

First of all, thank you for this excellent project! I found it very useful and decided to contribute back by adding support for the Hammerhead Karoo device.

This PR introduces modification of the device name to Garmin Edge 830 when uploading Hammerhead Karoo activities. Without this change, Hammerhead Karoo activity uploads function correctly, but the device name remains unchanged.

Please let me know if there's anything more you'd like adjusted or enhanced.

Thanks again for maintaining this great tool!

title: Fix issue with new TPV FIT file structure
description:
Fixes #22 

Issue was due to how the `FileIdMessage` was generated by TPV during a structured workout (compared to a free ride)

Changes:
- Change to generate FileIdMessage rather than editing in place to ensure device is properly set
- Also add FileCreator message (not sure if required)
- Bump version

title: Fix actions
fix version number
Rename project and make pip installable
description:
This project started as a simple script, so I never went through the hassle of setting up a pypi entry and making it pip installable and all that. This PR fixes that. Fixes #17.

Primary changes:
- Moves config file and `.garth` folder into user config and cache directories, using [platformdirs](https://github.com/tox-dev/platformdirs?tab=readme-ov-file)
- Added `pyproject.toml` for install with `uv` and publishing to pypi
- Adds GitHub actions to auto build and publish on tagged commits (pushes to testPyPI on any push)

title: Support fit files from Zwift
description:
This seems to fix the problem with Zwift files for me. This will close https://github.com/jat255/fit_file_uploader/issues/11

The problem seems to simply be that the ID 21 (Event) isn't supported somewhere in the tool chain. So we just skip it completely. 

The data stored in the event message looks pretty pointless so I think it's safe to remove. Maybe there is a better way to do this?

title: Fix: Write serial number and software version also to device_info if needed (for Karoo). fixes #84
description:
### Problem
Garmin Connect seemingly also relies on the information in device_info. If a mismatch exists, it won't show the device (see #84).

### Fix
Don't only edit the manufacturer and product in device_info but also serial_number and software_version fields.
The software version fields need to be made growable to write the changes.

Also only edit the fields if we can be sure that it is not a real sensor (like powermeter/HRM). This is checked by device_index which must be 0 (CREATOR in fit-tools).

Fixes #84
